text: {"summary":"Coding task v5-resolver-long-hard-2; entrypoint engine.solve(data), return complete replacement contents for allowlisted engine.py and rules.py only (Python 3.11, no third-party libraries/tools/network/workspace). Input packages maps names to rows {version:int,deps:list}; roots maps names to inclusive [min,max]. Install exactly the transitive dependency closure of roots. Every active dependency of a selected version must be installed within its inclusive range; version choice may require backtracking. Among feasible installations maximize the version vector in sorted ALL package-name order, using -1 for absent packages. If impossible, return {error:unsatisfiable}.\nPublic stages 1–2 passed (receipts: public_pass, checks 2 then 4). Stage 1 established closure and lexicographic selection; test expected only a:3 when a is root and unrelated packages exist. Stage 2 established inclusive root bounds and unsatisfiable result; expected a:2 for range [1,2]. Stage 3 is current, with two backtracking/dependency-closure fixtures: (a) root a:[1,2], expected {a:2,b:2,c:2,d:1,e:1}; (b) root a:[1,1], expected {a:1,b:2,c:2,d:2,e:2}. No stage-3 receipt is supplied. There are 8 stages total; remaining_actions reported as 28. Later-stage requirements are unknown.\nLatest checkpoint artifact contains engine.py and rules.py. engine.py recursively searches pending constraints, intersects dependency bounds, rejects conflicting/invalid chosen versions, and retains the lexicographically greatest complete assignment; returns {'error':'unsatisfiable'} when no assignment. rules.py provides bound parsing/intersection, range checking, and dependency parsing. Artifact also handles several dict/list/tuple constraint and dependency encodings, but the explicit task contract only guarantees the formats above. Initial artifact was a simple minimum-version-per-root chooser and is superseded. Trial notes are unverified; no wrong attempt should be invented."}
